record.original_question: If f (z) in S it is shown by Bombieri [105], that there exist constants cn such that for f (z) in S |Re (n − an )| ≤ cn Re (2 − a2 ). What is it the exact size of the constants cn ? Is it true that there exists dn such that  n − |an | ≤ dn 2 − |a2 | ? (E. Bombieri)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the class of holomorphic, univalent functions $f$ on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ normalized by
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n.$$
It is known that for each integer $n\ge 2$ there exists a constant $c_n>0$ such that, for every $f\in S$,
$$|\operatorname{Re}(n-a_n)|\le c_n\,\operatorname{Re}(2-a_2).$$
(a) Determine the exact (smallest possible) value of the constant $c_n$ for every $n\ge 2$.
(b) Decide whether, for each integer $n\ge 2$, there exists a constant $d_n>0$ such that, for every $f\in S$,
$$n-|a_n|\le d_n\,(2-|a_2|).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The sharp Bombieri numbers σ_{m,n} arising from the local behavior of S near the Koebe function were conjectured by Bombieri to give the constants in the inequality in (a). This conjectured value has been disproved in many cases: Leung disproved it for n=2 and all m≥3, and for n=3 and all odd m≥5; subsequent work extended counterexamples to all m>n≥2 with m,n of the same parity, and to certain mixed-parity cases. Thus the exact value of c_n is, in general, still not known, and the corresponding modulus version (b) also remains unresolved in full generality. The problem is therefore partially solved.

status_evidence.title: A Problem of Bombieri on Univalent Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Bombieri's conjecture on the coefficients of univalent functions and the constants σ_{m,n}.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured exact constants are the Bombieri numbers σ_{m,n}, but their values are not established in general.

status_evidence.title: On the Failure of Bombieri's Conjecture for Univalent Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Bombieri's conjectured value for the constants is shown to fail in many cases.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture identifying c_n with the Bombieri numbers is false in many cases, so the exact size of c_n remains open.

status_evidence.title: Some more counterexamples for Bombieri's conjecture on univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Provides further counterexamples to Bombieri's conjecture for additional index pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples extend to many (m,n) pairs, leaving the exact constants undetermined.
